QF.id: XIII Trading, Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_47

question.text: Which of the following correctly describes the stamp duty applicability on derivative contracts?

answer.text: Stamp duty is levied on derivative transactions and the rates are specified under the Indian Stamp Act as amended, applicable to both futures and options trades
Derivative contracts are exempt from stamp duty as they are not considered instruments of transfer under the Indian Stamp Act
Stamp duty applies only to physically settled derivatives, not to cash-settled derivatives
Stamp duty on derivatives is levied only at the state level and varies by state where the exchange is located

explanation.text: The Logic: Following the amendments to the Indian Stamp Act (effective July 2020), stamp duty is levied on derivative transactions at specified rates and is collected centrally by the stock exchange / clearing corporation on behalf of the state governments. Stamp duty applies to both futures and options trades irrespective of settlement mode. The Trap: Derivatives are NOT exempt from stamp duty post the 2020 amendment. The duty applies to both cash-settled and physically settled trades. Collection is centralised, not state-by-state at the exchange location. Note: Stamp duty applies to both futures and options across segments, but the rates vary by segment: currency and interest-rate derivatives are charged at 0.0001% on the buyer; equity futures at 0.002% on the buyer; equity options at 0.003% on the buyer.
